prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofing company for hurricane-rated roof replacement in Miami — the right contractor depends on your exact location, the roof type you want, your budget, and whether you need insurance-claim help. I can, however, tell you how to identify the best contractor for your job and what to verify before hiring.

What to look for
- Proper licensing and insurance
  - Florida DBPR (Contractor) license — get the license number and verify it on Florida’s DBPR website.
  - General liability and worker’s comp — ask for certificates naming you as additional insured during work if required.
- Experience with Miami-Dade / Florida Building Code and NOAs
  - Contractor should be familiar with Florida Building Code wind provisions and be able to provide Miami‑Dade County Notice of Acceptance (NOA) or other approvals for the materials and system they intend to install.
- Manufacturer certifications
  - Look for installers certified by major manufacturers (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning, TAMKO, etc.) or by the specific metal/tile manufacturer — certifications matter for full warranties.
- Hurricane-rated systems and correct installation
  - Ensure the proposed system is rated for high-wind (ask for design wind speed/uplift rating) and includes required details: secondary water barrier, proper fasteners/straps/clips, sealed penetrations, correct underlayment, and proper flashing.
- Local reputation & references
  - Check BBB, Google/Yelp reviews, and ask for recent Miami jobs and homeowner references you can contact.
- Written estimate and contract details
  - Scope of work, materials (brand/model, wind rating), permit responsibility, payment schedule, start/completion dates, cleanup, and written workmanship warranty.
- Permits and inspections
  - Contractor should obtain required permits and arrange final inspection — verify final permit closeout.

Questions to ask a roofer (sample)
- What is your Florida contractor license number? Can I see proof of liability and worker’s comp insurance?
- Have you done hurricane-rated roof replacements in my neighborhood? Can I get references?
- Are you a certified installer for the proposed product? Can you provide the NOA for this assembly?
- What wind speed/uplift rating will this roof have when completed?
- Who pulls the permits and who handles inspectors/permit closeout?
- What are the manufacturer warranty and your workmanship warranty? Are warranties transferable?

Materials to consider for hurricane-prone Miami
- Standing-seam metal and correctly attached concrete/terracotta tile are among the most wind-resistant options when installed per manufacturer specs and NOA requirements.
- High-wind rated architectural shingles can be an effective lower-cost solution if installed to code and with proper underlayment/attachments.
- Choose systems with Miami‑Dade NOA approvals when possible.

How to choose
- Get at least 3 written estimates that list the exact materials, attachments, and the NOA/manufacturer model.
- Prefer contractors who will provide a permit, final inspection, and a written workmanship warranty.
- Balance price with demonstrated experience on hurricane-rated systems and documented approvals.

If you want, I can:
- Look up and shortlist 3–5 reputed, licensed Miami roofers with experience in hurricane-rated replacements if you give your ZIP code.
- Or provide a printable checklist and a sample contract addendum you can give to contractors.

Which would you prefer?
